is arising out of the award dated 01.03.2019 passed by Ist Additional Member, MACT, Sardarpur, district Dhar in Claim Case No.55/2017 seeking enhancement of compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal.
2. The date of accident, negligence and the issue of liability are not in dispute and the findings recorded by the Tribunal in this regard are also not in question.

As per the findings of the Tribunal,
for the accidental death of Sukhram, the Tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs.10,15,000/- along with interest.

The breakup of the compensation amount is as under:
Loss of dependency -Rs.9,45,000/- (i.e.Rs.5000 x12=60000 40% FP=84000 - 1/4=63000 x 15 (multiplier)) Funeral expenses -Rs.15,000/-
 Loss of estate -Rs.15,000/-
 Loss of consortium -Rs.40,000/-
 -----------------
 TOTAL Rs.10,15,000/-
 ===========
3. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the Tribunal has committed an error in not awarding just and proper amount of compensation in the case as the amount awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side.

The income of the deceased Smt. Dakhabai vs Vijay Pratap Singh on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38258964/
2 assessed by the Tribunal is on the lower side, hence it should have been assessed as per Circular under the Minimum Wages Act/ Collector guidelines.

sentences.text:
The Tribunal has committed an error in not awarding filial as well as parental consortium in the case,
hence prays for just and proper amount of compensation in the case.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the Insurance Company argued in support of the impugned award and contended that the Claims Tribunal has rightly awarded the compensation amount in the case which does not call for any interference by this Court.

5. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.
6.
After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record, I find substance in the arguments advanced by the counsel for the appellant.
The Tribunal has not awarded filial as well as parental consortium in the case.
The income of the deceased assessed by the Tribunal is also on the lower side which ought to have been as per the guidelines framed under the Minimum Wages Act.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the arguments advanced by the counsel for the appellant as well as the evidence that came on record in the considered opinion of this Court, it would be just and proper to determine deceased's income as per Circular and notification issued under the Minimum Wages Act.
The accident was occurred on 22.11.2015.

Accordingly, as per the table of the minimum wages fixed by the Labour Department, Govt. of M.P,
the minimum wages of the deceased comes to Rs.6,575/- per month.

Hence, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal deserves to be enhanced and is modified as under:
Loss of dependency -Rs.12,42,675/- (i.e. Rs.6,575 x 12=78,900 40% FP=1,10,460 - 1/4 personal expenses=82,845 x 15 (multiplier)) Loss of consortium -Rs.2,00,000/-
 Other conventional heads -Rs.30,000/-
 --------------------
 TOTAL Rs.14,72,675/-
 =============
7.
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.14,72,675/- as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.10,15,000/-.
Accordingly, the appellant is entitled to an additional sum of Rs.4,57,675/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
8. In the result, the appeal is partly allowed by enhancing the compensation amount by a sum of Rs.4,57,675/-.
The enhanced amount shall bear interest at the same rate as awarded by the Tribunal.
The other findings recorded by the Tribunal shall remain intact.
